topics.title: Spelling: Double letters (part 1)
topics.hook: Say it in your “spelling voice”, one chunk at a time: ac-com-mo-date, com-mit-tee. You’ll hear where the doubles go.
topics.intro: These words are on the official Year 5 and 6 list. For each one, notice the tricky part, then cover it and write it from memory.
topics.teach: Pick one word from today and explain its tricky part.
topics.talk: Ask her to spell one of this week’s words and say what the tricky part is.

topics.title: Spelling: Double letters (part 2)

topics.title: Spelling: Silent letters and hidden sounds
topics.hook: Say it the silly way in your head (yac-ht, mus-cle, gov-ern-ment) so the hidden letters can’t escape.

topics.hook: -ant goes with -ance, -ent goes with -ence: relevant → relevance, convenient → convenience.

topics.title: Spelling: Tricky words I–V
topics.hook: Chop it into chunks and spot a word you know: re-COG-nise, SIGN-ature, ve-HI-cle.
topics.intro: These words are on the official Year 5 and 6 list. For each one, notice the tricky part, then cover it and write it from memory.
topics.teach: Pick one word from today and explain its tricky part.
topics.talk: Ask her to spell one of this week’s words and say what the tricky part is.

items.sentence: The hotel can ___ forty guests.
items.explain: Two c’s and two m’s: ac-com-mo-date.
items.learn: **accommodate**: Two c’s and two m’s: ac-com-mo-date.
items.hook: Accommodate has room for two c’s and two m’s.
items.example: B&B signs say “Accommodation available”: check the double c and double m next time you pass one.

items.sentence: Will you ___ me to the shop?
items.hook: ac + company: when you accompany someone, you keep them company.

items.sentence: ___ to the forecast, it will rain.
The ___ goose chased us across the field.
items.hook: Aggressive geese hiss: double g, double s.

items.sentence: It was ___ that nobody had cleaned up.
items.explain: ap + par + ent: double p, single r, ends -ent.
items.learn: **apparent**: ap + par + ent: double p, single r, ends -ent.
items.hook: It’s apparent there’s a parent in it: ap-PARENT.

items.sentence: I really ___ your help.
A label was ___ to the parcel.
items.explain: Double t, and no t before ch: at-tached.
items.learn: **attached**: Double t, and no t before ch: at-tached.
items.hook: A tack keeps it attached: at + TACH + ed, with no extra t.

items.sentence: The school ___ met to plan the fair.
items.clue: a group chosen to make decisions
items.explain: Double m, double t, double e.
items.learn: **committee**: Double m, double t, double e.
items.hook: Committee: Many Meetings Take Time, Everyone’s Exhausted (double m, double t, double e).

items.sentence: Dolphins ___ using clicks and whistles.
Our ___ held a street party.
items.clue: the people living in one area
items.hook: A community needs unity: comm + UNITY.

items.sentence: I ___ with a pen pal in France.
items.clue: to write letters to each other
items.hook: cor + RESPOND: when you correspond, you respond to each other’s letters.

items.sentence: Please don’t ___ me in front of my friends.
items.hook: Embarrass: really red and so shy (double r, double s).

items.sentence: Don’t ___; it was only a small spider.
items.clue: to make something sound bigger than it is
items.hook: Don’t exaggerate the g’s: there are exactly two, ex-AGG-er-ate.

items.sentence: You did an ___ job on that poster.
items.hook: Excellent has two l’s, like two thumbs up, and ends -ent.

items.sentence: Seagulls ___ people eating chips on the beach.
items.hook: Unlike embarrass, harass has just one r: ha-rass. It still has a double s.

items.sentence: Come here ___!
items.explain: Double m, and keep the e: immediate + ly.
items.learn: **immediately**: Double m, and keep the e: immediate + ly.
items.hook: The MEDIA report it immediately: im-MEDIA-tely.

items.sentence: It is rude to ___ someone who is speaking.
items.clue: to break in while someone is talking
items.hook: inter + rupt (break): the double r is where you break in.

items.sentence: We had a ___ time at the seaside.
items.hook: British English doubles the l: marve-LL-ous.
items.example: American books and websites write “marvelous” with one l. In a UK spelling test, use two.

items.sentence: Is it ___ to bring a coat?
items.hook: Necessary: one collar, two sleeves (one c, two s’s).

items.sentence: The new family will ___ the empty house.
items.clue: to live in or fill a space

items.sentence: Earthquakes ___ along fault lines.
items.explain: Double c, single r (but occurred, occurring).
items.learn: **occur**: Double c, single r (but occurred, occurring).
items.hook: Occur, but occurred and occurring: double the r when you add an ending.

items.sentence: This trip is a great ___ to learn.
items.clue: a good chance to do something
items.hook: A ship in PORT has the opportunity to sail: op-PORT-unity.

items.sentence: My favourite TV ___ starts at six.
items.clue: a show on TV or radio
items.hook: A TV programme has -mme; only computer code is a “program”.
items.example: TV guides print “programme”, but even in Britain you write a computer “program”.

items.sentence: I ___ this book to anyone who likes mysteries.
items.explain: One c, double m: re + commend.
items.learn: **recommend**: One c, double m: re + commend.
items.hook: re + commend: one c, double m.

items.sentence: Is there ___ food for everyone?
items.hook: Sufficient works like efficient: double f, then -cient.

items.sentence: Can I ___ a better plan?
items.hook: Say it slowly, “sug-jest”, and hear both g’s.

items.sentence: A white ___ sailed into the harbour.
items.clue: a sailing boat used for racing or holidays
items.hook: Say it “yac-ht” in your spelling voice to remember the hidden ch.
items.example: Look at the boats’ names in a harbour or on a “Yacht Club” sign.

items.sentence: Your heart is a ___.
items.clue: body tissue that makes you move
items.hook: Hear the hidden c in muscular: mus-CU-lar → muscle.

items.sentence: “Cat” and “hat” ___.
items.clue: to end with the same sound
items.explain: rh at the start, y in the middle.
items.learn: **rhyme**: rh at the start, y in the middle.
items.hook: Rhyme starts like rhythm: rh, then a y.

items.sentence: Clap along to the ___ of the song.
items.hook: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move.

items.sentence: My ___ told me to own up.
items.clue: the inner sense of right and wrong
items.hook: Your conscience is the science of right and wrong: con + SCIENCE.

items.sentence: The patient was ___ and talking.
items.hook: con + SCI + ous: the “sci” from science again.

items.sentence: She speaks three ___ languages.
items.hook: A foreign king REIGNS over another land: fo-REIGN.

items.sentence: The ___ makes laws for the country.
items.clue: the group of people who run a country
items.hook: Government: govern + ment. You govern a country, so keep the n.

items.sentence: We must protect the ___.
items.hook: Environment has iron in it: env-IRON-ment.

items.sentence: Laws are debated in ___.
items.clue: the group that makes a country’s laws
items.hook: Parliament: I am in parliament (par-l-I-AM-ent).
items.example: Laws for the UK are debated in the Houses of Parliament, home of Big Ben.

items.sentence: The ___ marched across the square.
My ___ is rumbling.
items.clue: where food goes after you swallow it
items.hook: Tom has a stomach ache: s-TOM-ACH.

items.sentence: Today is my ___ birthday.
items.explain: twelve → twelfth: the v becomes f, then add th.
items.learn: **twelfth**: twelve → twelfth: the v becomes f, then add th.
items.hook: Twelve → twelfth: drop the e, turn the v into f, then add th.
items.example: Shakespeare’s play Twelfth Night is named after the twelfth night after Christmas.

items.sentence: Give your room a ___ clean.
items.hook: Be thorough and rub off every ROUGH bit: tho-ROUGH.

items.sentence: We waited in a long ___.
items.explain: q-u-e-u-e: five letters, but you only hear “kyoo”.
items.learn: **queue**: q-u-e-u-e: five letters, but you only hear “kyoo”.
items.hook: The letters u-e-u-e wait in a queue behind the q.

items.sentence: A flash of ___ lit up the sky.
items.clue: a flash of light in a storm
items.hook: Lightning has no e. Lightening means making something lighter.
items.example: A hairdresser offers hair lightening; a thunderstorm brings lightning.

items.sentence: I ___ you will love this film.
items.hook: A GUARd guarantees your safety: GUAR-an-tee.

items.sentence: Swimming is my favourite ___ activity.
items.hook: “i before e” only rules the ee sound. Leisure says “lezh”, so ei is fine.
items.example: A sports centre is often called a “Leisure Centre”: look at the sign.

items.sentence: The buzzing fly was a real ___.
For your ___, the shop is open late.
Scientists debated the ___ of the giant squid.
The heavy bag was a ___ on the hike.
items.clue: something that gets in the way
items.hook: Hinder drops its e: hind-rance, never “hinderance”.

items.sentence: Only include ___ facts in your answer.
items.hook: Relevant ends -ant, like elephANT.

items.sentence: We ate pizza at a new ___.
items.clue: a place where you buy and eat meals
items.hook: You REST, then you RANT about the bill: REST-au-RANT.

items.sentence: The ___ puppy chewed my shoe.
items.hook: A mischief-maker is mischievous: f turns to v, and there’s no extra i (not “mischievious”).

items.sentence: The storm was ___ for the farmers.
items.hook: Disaster drops its e: disastrous, never “disasterous”.

items.sentence: Her ___ made her open the box.
items.clue: a strong wish to know something
items.hook: Curious drops its u: curi-OS-ity, never “curiousity”.

items.sentence: He is an ___ photographer, not a professional.
items.clue: someone who does something for fun, not pay
items.hook: An amateur does it for love (Latin amare, to love), not for money.

items.sentence: It was a ___ to meet the author.
items.hook: It’s VILE to put a d in privilege: pri-VILE-ge.

items.sentence: She made a ___ to help her family.
items.clue: giving something up for something else

items.sentence: Judging someone by their accent is ___.
items.clue: an unfair opinion formed in advance
items.hook: pre + judice: to judge before you know.

items.sentence: Don’t ___ with the experiment.
items.clue: to get involved where not wanted

items.sentence: We need a ___ answer by Friday.
items.hook: Definite has finite in it: de-FINITE.

items.sentence: The thirsty traveller was ___ for water.
items.hook: Say “des-PER-ate” in your spelling voice to hear the e before the r.

items.sentence: Which ___ does a whale belong to?
The old ___ had mossy gravestones.
items.clue: a place where people are buried
items.hook: Three e’s, like the “eee!” you scream walking past a cemetery at night.

items.sentence: The ___ height in our class is 140 cm.
This jacket was a ___ at half price.
items.hook: You GAIN when you get a bargain: bar + GAIN.
items.example: Shop windows shout “Bargain!” in the sales. Check they’ve spelled it right.

items.sentence: Look the word up in a ___.
The club ___ wrote the minutes.
items.clue: someone who writes letters and keeps records
items.hook: A secretary keeps a SECRET: secret + ary.

items.sentence: A carrot is a root ___.
items.hook: Put the VEG on the TABLE: veg-e-TABLE.

items.sentence: The ___ dropped below zero.
items.clue: how hot or cold something is
items.hook: Your TEMPER rises with the temperature: temper + a + ture.
items.example: Weather forecasts give the temperature in °C.

items.sentence: It ___ rains in Manchester.
Tadpoles ___ into frogs.
items.explain: No e at the end: develop.
items.learn: **develop**: No e at the end: develop.
items.hook: Develop has no e at the end, but envelope does.

items.sentence: She won the spelling ___.
items.explain: compete → competition: e changes to i.
items.learn: **competition**: compete → competition: e changes to i.
items.hook: Enter your PET in a competition: com-PET-ition.

items.sentence: Write an ___ of how a volcano erupts.
items.clue: something that makes a thing clear
items.hook: PLAN your explanation: ex-PLAN-ation (explain drops its i).

items.sentence: Check the ___ of this word.
items.clue: the way a word is said
items.hook: There’s a NUN in pronunciation, and no “noun”.

items.sentence: If you practise, you will ___ your goal.
items.hook: i before e except after c, when the sound is ee: achieve, field, but receive. Watch for exceptions like seize and weird.

items.sentence: We visited an ___ castle.
items.hook: Ancient has “cie”, but that’s fine: “i before e except after c” is only for the ee sound.

items.sentence: Tickets are ___ online.
items.clue: able to be used or got

items.sentence: There was an ___ silence.
I have a purple ___ on my knee.
items.clue: a mark on the skin after a knock
items.hook: A bruised FRUIT has ui too: br-UI-se.

items.sentence: The new rule caused a lot of ___.
It is easy to ___ but harder to help.
items.hook: A CRITIC criticises: critic + ise.

items.sentence: She was ___ to finish the race.
Put the PE ___ away.
items.clue: the things needed for an activity
items.hook: equip + ment, one p. Only equipped and equipping double it.

items.sentence: I love fruit, ___ strawberries.
items.hook: It’s especially SPECIAL: e + special + ly.

items.sentence: That voice sounds ___.
items.hook: Your FAMILy is familiar: famil + iar.

items.sentence: There are ___ children in the choir.
items.hook: Forty has lost its u: four → forty, but fourteen keeps it.

items.sentence: The spy kept her ___ secret.
Each ___ has a locker.
French is a beautiful ___.
items.clue: a system of words people use to communicate
items.hook: You can learn a langUAGE at any AGE: lang + u + age.

items.sentence: Our ___ has a cat called Biscuit.
items.hook: Neighbour starts like eight: n-EIGH-bour.
items.example: “Neighbourhood Watch” signs on lamp posts use the British -our spelling.

items.sentence: Can you ___ your mum to let us go?
Running is good ___ exercise.
items.hook: ph sounds like f, as in phone and photo: PHYS-ical.

items.sentence: Nursing is a caring ___.
items.clue: a job that needs special training
items.hook: Like professor: one f, double s.

items.sentence: I didn’t ___ you with your new haircut.
items.clue: to know someone or something again
items.hook: The COGs in your brain whirr when you recognise someone: re-COG-nise.

items.sentence: The parrot sat on the pirate’s ___.
items.clue: the joint between the arm and neck
items.hook: Shoulder starts like should: sh-OULD-er (O U Lucky Duck).

items.sentence: Write your ___ at the bottom.
items.clue: your name written in your own way
items.hook: Your signature is your SIGN: keep the g you hear in “signal”.

items.sentence: Please accept my ___ apologies.
items.explain: sin + cere. Sincerely keeps the e.
items.learn: **sincere**: sin + cere. Sincerely keeps the e.

items.sentence: The dove is a ___ of peace.
items.clue: a sign that stands for something
items.hook: A symbol is a sign; a cymbal crashes in a band. Both use y.

items.sentence: The solar ___ has eight planets.
items.clue: a set of parts that work together

items.sentence: The shop sells a ___ of sweets.
items.hook: A variety of VARIous things: vari + ety.

items.sentence: A tractor is a farm ___.
items.clue: something used for carrying people or goods
items.hook: Say HI to the vehicle: ve-HI-cle.
